metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU, Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (Quote: 'computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)')

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China. Includes 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. used to calibrate simulation driving behaviors.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper explicitly states the data is available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle coordinates from raw video to create position matrices. Matrices from three consecutive time steps are stacked to represent the traffic state, with down-sampling applied for efficiency.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, generic vision tools unnamed, key state dimensions and stacking logic stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: A multitask learning strategy is implemented in the training process to improve learning efficiency.
nodes_process.description: Trains a Q-network using Algorithm 1. The network uses three CNN layers and two FC layers to simultaneously estimate Q-values and predict traffic metrics. Uses Adam optimizer and experience replay for stability.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all hyperparams and architecture detailed, hardware and optimizer specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained model in a 20-run simulation experiment on a freeway segment. Comparisons are made against no-control and PI-ALINEA baselines based on travel time, speed, and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulator named, setup parameters and speed limits explicitly stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Divides the control area into eight subareas and systematically removes data from each subarea to measure the resulting impact on travel time stability.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, logic for spatial partitioning and data removal defined but results shown as aggregate boxplots.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence of the episode reward over 10^6 training frames during the DRL training process.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Methods and parameters specified; however, the raw 'empirical data' for simulation calibration is not provided as a public URL.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence of the mean travel time over 10^6 training frames during the DRL training process.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training process and parameters (Table 1) are well-defined, but the exact input traffic data source is proprietary.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mainline vehicle travel times across three scenarios: No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL, shown as quartiles over time.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: The comparison procedure is clear and SUMO is open source, but the specific traffic volume dataset is available only upon request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean travel times (seconds) and percentage improvement for 20 individual simulation runs comparing No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Highly detailed per-run results provided. Reproducibility limited only by lack of public access to the raw calibration data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing speed distribution across distance and time for (a) no-control, (b) PI-ALINEA, and (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plausible derivation from SUMO simulation, though exact plotting binning/interpolation details are omitted.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Quartiles of vehicle queue lengths at the on-ramp over time for the three experimental scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Standard metric from SUMO; procedure is fully specified.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of traffic volume (veh/h) downstream of the merging area at 5-minute intervals for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Well-defined output from microscopic simulation; coherent with reported traffic demand.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Perturbation analysis showing the impact on mean travel time when video data from specific road subareas (1-8) is missing.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: The perturbation methodology (division into 8 subareas) is clearly illustrated and described.
